findings: The book writes '4-hyrodxy aryl anion (C6H5-)'; the synthon is the 4-hydroxyphenyl anion. Phenol is nitrated with 'HNO3, H2SO4'; dilute nitric acid suffices for phenol (Chapter 22) and gives 2- and 4-nitrophenol.

The book makes salicylic acid from phenol and CO2 at high temperature and pressure; the lesson adds that in practice sodium phenoxide is used. The Quick Check questions are printed without answers; the lesson's answers were derived for it and need the second-person review.

In the paracetamol retrosynthesis, Step III (FGI) is printed with an ordinary reaction arrow from 4-aminophenol to 4-nitrophenol, the reverse of a real reaction; the redrawn scheme uses the retrosynthetic arrow, and the Roman Urdu note explains it.
